title: Pre-filtering with security filters
summary: Each chunk stores the identities allowed to read it, and the app adds a search.in filter built from the caller's identities. The engine filters before it ranks. This is the GA, any-API-version pattern in Azure AI Search.
useIf: Permissions map to users or groups that you can copy onto every chunk, and a sync lag of minutes to hours is acceptable.
avoidIf: Revocation must take effect in seconds, or access is decided by rules (deny, sharing links) that cannot be flattened into allow lists.

explain.md: A security filter is a plain string-comparison technique: a `Collection(Edm.String)` field on each chunk lists the principals allowed to read it, and the query carries a filter such as `group_ids/any(g:search.in(g, 'id1, id2'))`. It works on any API version and is GA [[r13]]. Because the filter runs before ranking, top-k holds only allowed chunks and recall stays stable.

blocks.title: Index action that patches only the ACL field

explain.md: Design the field with care. **The pattern has no authentication**: the principal is only a string, so your code must derive it from a validated token and build the filter server side. `retrievable: false` only hides the field from responses and is not field-level security. Update ACLs with `merge` or `mergeOrUpload`, so a revocation can patch one field without re-embedding [[r13]].

`search.in` equals a chain of `eq ... or` but is faster. The docs report sub-second responses with hundreds or thousands of values, no explicit cap on the count, a limit set by the maximum request size, and latency that grows with the number of values [[r14]]. Use POST: a GET URL is limited to 8 KB and the payload to 16 MB [[r20]]. For vector queries set `vectorFilterMode` to `preFilter` explicitly [[tr19]].

explain.title: Empty means nobody, never everybody
explain.md: Store an explicit public marker (for example a `public` entry that every caller's list includes). If an empty ACL means public, a failed ACL capture at ingest silently publishes the document.

whereToUse: Enterprise search where permissions are exported from a directory or file share
Multi-department assistants with a department or role tag per chunk
Shared multi-tenant indexes, with the tenant id as one more filtered field
Any system whose identity provider is not Entra, so native token-based ACLs do not apply

use: Permissions reduce to allow lists of users or groups
You need GA and a stable API
You own group resolution and ACL sync
avoid: Deny rules, sharing links and guests that cannot be flattened
Revocation in seconds with only a pull indexer
Callers with so many effective groups that the filter grows past the request budget
flips: Revocation must be instant: add a live check on sensitive hits
Content is in ADLS Gen2 or SharePoint and preview is acceptable: consider native ACLs
A caller can hold thousands of groups: send only the groups that appear on documents, or switch to roles

pitfalls.symptom: A revoked user still sees a document
pitfalls.cause: The index was not updated after the ACL change
pitfalls.fix: Push a merge on change events, bound sync lag, and test revocation with a canary user

pitfalls.symptom: A document with no ACL shows to everyone
pitfalls.cause: An empty field was treated as public
pitfalls.fix: Require an explicit public marker and fail closed on empty

pitfalls.symptom: Filter requests are slow or rejected
pitfalls.cause: Thousands of group ids in one filter, sent as a GET
pitfalls.fix: Send POST, expand membership server side and send only groups that appear on documents

pitfalls.cause: The client sends the filter string
pitfalls.fix: Build the filter only on the server from a validated token

scenarios.title: Custom identity system, GA required
scenarios.situation: A product uses its own directory service, not Entra. Each user belongs to about 120 groups. The assistant goes to production next quarter and requires a supported API. A revoked grant must stop working within 15 minutes.
unknowns: Does the directory emit change events?
How many chunks does one ACL change touch?
scenarios.question: How do you enforce permissions?

options.name: Native ACL filters driven by the user's Entra token
options.why: They are preview, rely on Entra identities and are not recommended for production [[r11]].
options.tradeoff: Right when content sits in ADLS Gen2 or SharePoint with Entra identities and a pilot is acceptable.

options.name: Security filter, with change events from the directory triggering a merge of the ACL field
options.why: GA, works with any identity, and a push merge lands as soon as the change event arrives, well inside 15 minutes.
options.tradeoff: You own the change feed and group resolution.

options.name: Security filter refreshed by a nightly full rebuild
options.tradeoff: Up to a day of stale grants, which misses the 15-minute target.

flips.then: Keep the filter and add a live check on sensitive hits.

flips.if: The identity system becomes Entra and preview is allowed
flips.then: Native ACLs remove your group-expansion code.

scenarios.takeaway: GA plus a custom identity system points to security filters with push updates.

scenarios.title: Callers with thousands of effective groups
scenarios.situation: Large customers have callers who hold up to 3,000 effective groups through nesting. The index has 40 million chunks and documents carry a few hundred distinct principal ids in total.
unknowns: Which principals actually appear on documents?
scenarios.question: How do you build the filter?

options.name: Send all 3,000 ids in a GET request URL
options.why: A GET URL is limited to 8 KB, and latency grows with the value count [[r20]].
options.tradeoff: Fine for callers with a handful of groups.

options.name: Intersect the caller's groups with the set of principals that appear on documents, and send that set by POST
options.why: Groups no document references cannot grant access, so the filter shrinks to what matters. This is design reasoning, not a vendor feature.
options.tradeoff: You maintain the principal set at ingest and refresh it when new principals appear.

options.name: Send all 3,000 ids by POST
options.why: The docs report sub-second results with hundreds or thousands of values [[r14]].
options.tradeoff: Latency still grows with count and payload size.

flips.then: Send the full list by POST and skip the intersection.

flips.if: Access can be expressed as a few roles
flips.then: Use role claims and shrink the filter further.

scenarios.takeaway: Shrink the filter to principals that appear on documents.

scenarios.title: Public documents and failed ACL capture
scenarios.situation: Some documents are readable by everyone and others by groups. A connector sometimes fails to read a file's permissions and writes an empty list. The team treats an empty list as public.
unknowns: How often does ACL capture fail?
Is there an alert on empty ACLs?
scenarios.question: How do you change the design?

options.name: Keep empty as public and alert on empty lists
options.why: An unnoticed failure publishes restricted documents in the meantime.
options.tradeoff: Acceptable only when every document is public by design.

options.name: Write an explicit public marker for public documents, treat empty as nobody and quarantine unknown ACLs
options.why: A failed capture hides the document instead of publishing it.
options.tradeoff: Failures cause missing results until fixed, so alert on quarantined counts.

options.name: Re-read permissions from the source on every query
options.tradeoff: Adds latency and source load and discards the point of the index filter.

flips.then: Keep the marker and add a cheap per-hit check for the restricted minority.
Push ACL merges on change events.

quiz.q: Setting retrievable to false on the ACL field gives which protection?
options: Field-level security: callers cannot filter on it
It hides the field from responses only. The filter is the control
It encrypts the stored principal ids
quiz.explain: retrievable: false keeps the field out of search results. Filtering still works, and it is not field-level security. It does not encrypt or make anything read-only.

quiz.q: Which statements about the security filter pattern are correct? Choose all that apply.
options: It works with any API version
The ACL field can be updated with merge or mergeOrUpload
The filter is applied before ranking
quiz.explain: The pattern is API-agnostic, ACLs can be patched with merge actions and the filter runs before ranking. It does not authenticate anyone: your code must derive the principal from a validated token.

flashcards.front: Which field settings does a security filter use in Azure AI Search?
flashcards.back: A Collection(Edm.String) field with filterable true and retrievable false. retrievable false hides it from responses but is not field-level security.

flashcards.front: Does the security filter pattern authenticate users?
flashcards.back: No. The principal is only a string. Your code must validate the token, resolve identities and build the filter on the server.

flashcards.front: Why store an explicit public marker?
flashcards.back: If empty means public, a failed ACL capture publishes a restricted document. With empty meaning nobody, the failure hides it instead.
